events.title: Senate 'skinny repeal' fails 49-51; ACA-exposed hospitals and Medicaid insurers keep their 2017 rally
events.summary: In the early hours of July 28, 2017 John McCain, Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski voted no on the 'skinny' Obamacare repeal, ending the seven-year Republican repeal effort at 49-51. Hospital operators (HCA, Tenet, Community Health) and exchange/Medicaid insurers (Centene, Molina) had traded all year as repeal proxies, jumping on each failure (Tenet +7.4% and Community Health +9.5% on March 24 when the House bill was pulled; Centene hit a record $87.94 on July 25). The vote removed the coverage-loss overhang for the group, although HCA's guidance cut three days earlier capped the hospital names.
events.evidence: Senate rejected the Health Care Freedom Act 49-51 on 2017-07-28; Tenet +7.4% and Community Health +9.5% on the prior repeal failure (2017-03-24).

events.title: Aetna-Humana ($37bn) and Anthem-Cigna ($54bn): the summer-2015 insurer merger wave
events.summary: Aetna agreed to buy Humana for $230 a share in cash and stock (about $37bn) on July 3, 2015, and Anthem agreed to buy Cigna for about $54bn on July 24, deals that would have cut the five national insurers to three. Humana rose as much as 4% and Aetna fell as much as 6% on announcement day, while Cigna fell from $154.36 to $145.91 and Anthem from $155.23 to $150.76 on July 24 as the Street doubted antitrust approval. Humana closed at $181.76, far below the offer value, a merger-arb spread that foreshadowed the DOJ suits of July 2016.

events.title: Courts block Aetna-Humana and Anthem-Cigna; horizontal insurer consolidation ends
events.summary: Judge John Bates blocked Aetna's acquisition of Humana on antitrust grounds on January 23, 2017 (Humana closed up 2.2% at $205.02, Aetna down about 2.5% near $119), and a second federal judge blocked Anthem-Cigna on February 9. Aetna and Humana terminated on February 14 with Aetna paying a $1bn break fee, and Cigna sued Anthem to exit. The rulings were widely expected and the stocks shrugged, but they rerouted managed-care capital into vertical deals (CVS-Aetna in December 2017, Cigna-Express Scripts in March 2018).

events.title: Drug distributors settle the Ohio opioid bellwether for $260m hours before trial
events.summary: McKesson, Cardinal Health and AmerisourceBergen agreed to pay a combined $215m, and Teva $20m in cash plus Suboxone, to Cuyahoga and Summit counties on the morning the first federal opioid trial was due to start. The deal removed a near-term binary that had weighed on distributor multiples through 2018-19 and signalled that a global settlement framework was achievable. Walgreens did not settle and remained a defendant.

events.title: $26bn global opioid settlement lifts the liability overhang from MCK, CAH and ABC
events.summary: State attorneys general unveiled a $26bn agreement on July 21, 2021: McKesson $7.9bn, Cardinal Health $6.4bn and AmerisourceBergen $6.4bn over 18 years, plus Johnson & Johnson $5bn over nine years, with an independent monitor and data sharing. The deal became effective on February 25, 2022 after enough states and localities joined. Capping the liability at a known, multi-decade payment stream let the drug distributors re-rate as steady GLP-1 and specialty-volume compounders rather than litigation risks.

events.title: 2012 housing recovery: PulteGroup +169% as builders lead the market
events.summary: After six years of bust, home prices rose for eight straight months through October 2012 (CoreLogic), QE3 in September pushed mortgage rates to record lows, and homebuilders became the year's best-performing group. PulteGroup gained 169%, Lennar 92% and Toll Brothers 54% in 2012, and the group kept rallying into early 2013 before the taper tantrum. Capital that had avoided housing since 2006 rotated back into builders, building products and home improvement.

events.title: Fed's 50bp cut: XBI's 'anticlimactic' reaction after a six-month pre-rally
events.summary: The Fed opened its easing cycle with a 50bp cut on September 18, 2024, the largest since 2008. XBI spiked about $2 at the 2pm announcement, closed flat near $100, and rose about 2% the next morning; analysts called the reaction a net positive but anticlimactic because SMID biotech had already rallied hard from its spring lows in anticipation. The episode showed that cost-of-capital trades in long-duration biotech are front-run rather than bought on the news.

Horton, PulteGroup and Toll 1-3%, with the S&P 500 Homebuilding index already up more than 30% year to date against 17% for the S&P 500. The rally proved to be the top: the 10-year yield rose roughly 80bp over the following two months and mortgage rates went back above 7%, so the group gave back its gains into early 2025. It is the clearest recent example of builders pricing the easing cycle before it arrived.

Precision scheduled railroading then spread to Union Pacific (Unified Plan 2020, 2018), Norfolk Southern and Kansas City Southern, and rails re-rated on falling operating ratios through 2019 even as carload volumes declined. Harrison died in December 2017 but the margin playbook outlived him.

CBRE reported record revenue, earnings and free cash flow for 2021 (GAAP EPS $5.41, +143%; free cash flow $2.2bn), and brokers rallied through the year. events.title: Semiconductor bottom of December 2018: Nvidia's crypto glut, then a 60% SOX year
events.summary: The SOX fell about 25% from October to late December 2018 (-15.5% in Q4) as the trade war, Fed hikes and a crypto-mining inventory glut hit the group; Nvidia lost 54% in Q4 alone and Micron bottomed at $28.39 on December 26. events.title: The 2016-18 DRAM supercycle peaks: Micron -56% from its June 2018 high
events.summary: Two years of DRAM and NAND price inflation driven by cloud over-ordering took Micron from under $10 in 2016 to an intraday high of $64.66 in June 2018. Hyperscalers then worked down inventory through 2018, Micron guided below expectations on September 20, 2018, and the stock fell 56% to $28.39 by December 26 (down 22.8% for the calendar year). Fiscal 2019 revenue fell 23% to $23.4bn, yet the shares rose 69% in 2019 as the market looked through the trough, the classic memory-cycle pattern.

events.title: Moody's strips the last Aaa: 30-year Treasury tops 5%, bond-proxy REITs and utilities wobble
events.summary: Moody's cut the U.S. to Aa1 after the close on May 16, 2025, citing deficits heading toward 9% of GDP by 2035, the last of the three agencies to remove the top rating. The 30-year yield rose above 5% (5.02%) on May 19 and S&P futures fell 1.1% before the index closed up 0.1%, so the equity damage was concentrated in rate-sensitive groups rather than the market. For net-lease REITs and utilities, the move reinforced the term-premium problem: long yields at 5% leave dividend yields of 4-6% without a spread, a theme that recurred in the 2026 selloff.

events.title: Walmart's investor day: -10%, its worst day since 1988, on wage and e-commerce investment

events.title: Abqaiq-Khurais attack removes 5.7m b/d: oil's largest one-day jump in a decade, faded within weeks
events.summary: Drone and missile strikes on September 14, 2019 knocked out 5.7m b/d of Saudi output, about 5% of world supply and the largest gross supply loss on record. Brent rose about 15% on September 16, its biggest single-day increase in a decade (nearly 20% at the open), and U.S. energy stocks jumped while the broad market fell. Saudi Arabia restored output by the end of the month and crude gave back the entire spike within two weeks, a demonstration of how little geopolitical premium the market would hold with shale growing and energy at a record-low index weight.
